335319.title: Two-scale asymptotic normality for distinct-part core-partition sizes
335319.literal_statement:
Let $X_{d,n}$ be the size of a uniformly random $(n,dn-1)$-core partition with distinct parts, with mean $\mu_{d,n}$ and standard deviation $\sigma_{d,n}$. For each fixed $n$, consider the standardized variable $(X_{d,n}-\mu_{d,n})/\sigma_{d,n}$ as $d$ tends to infinity.

**Two-scale normality conjecture.** For each fixed $n$, the distribution of $X_{d,n}$ is not asymptotically normal; in fact, $(X_{d,n}-\mu_{d,n})/\sigma_{d,n}$ tends to some abnormal distribution $X_n$ as $d\to\infty$. However, $X_n$ is asymptotically normal: $(X_n-\mu)/\sigma$ tends to the standard normal distribution as $n\to\infty$.

The conjecture distinguishes the limits in $d$ and $n$: the first limit is non-normal for fixed $n$, while the resulting family is expected to become normal as $n$ grows. The source supports this with computed standardized moments but gives no proof or resolution.
335319.ordinary_assessment: Fixed-n limit requires a continuous abacus/order-ideal size law and then an n-limit CLT. Moment data do not supply either convergence or uniform moment control. n1 zero variance is only a domain endpoint issue, not a discovery.

373744.title: The layered-permutation exponential-growth conjecture
373744.literal_statement:
For $w\in S_n$, let $\Upsilon_w=\mathfrak{S}_w(1^n)$, and let “$w$ layered” mean that $w$ is a layered permutation. Define

$$
L_n=\max_{w\text{ layered}}\Upsilon_w,\qquad M_n=\max_{w\in S_n}\Upsilon_w.
$$

**Layered exponential-growth conjecture.** The two maxima have the same exponential growth rate:

$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{1}{n^2}\log_2 M_n
=
\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{1}{n^2}\log_2 L_n
\approx 0.29.
$$

Equivalently, any improvement over layered permutations is subexponential in $n^2$.

The value of the layered limit was computed by Morales, Pak, and Panova, while the equality with the unrestricted limit is not proved in the source. The paper presents this as an expectation, so its status is open.
373744.ordinary_assessment: Needs equality of two n² logarithmic growth rates, not isolated maximizers. No injection/weight domination of arbitrary pipe dreams by layered objects with exp(o(n²)) loss obtained.

366031.title: The superexponential growth and exponential decay conjecture for Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials
366031.literal_statement:
For each $n$, let $\mathrm{num}_{n}$ be the number of distinct polynomials among $\{\mathrm{P}_{w}\mid w\in\mathrm{S}_{n}\}$, and let $\mathrm{num}_{n}^{\%}$ be the ratio of this number to the size of the corresponding multiset. **Growth and decay conjecture.** The number of distinct Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials grows superexponentially, meaning

$$
\mathrm{num}_{n}\in\Omega(\gamma^{n})\quad\text{for all }\gamma\in\mathbb{R}_{>1},
$$

and the percentage of distinct polynomials decays exponentially, meaning

$$
\mathrm{num}_{n}^{\%}\in O(\delta^{n})\quad\text{for some }\delta\in(0,1).
$$

The claim is based on computed data for $n$ through $11$ and concerns the asymptotic distribution of distinct first-row Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials.
366031.ordinary_assessment: Both superexponential distinct-count lower bound and exponentially small ratio required. Block products can collide and do not give injectivity or factorial-scale upper savings.

359272.title: Asymptotic equivalence of full and Gaussian maxT power
359272.literal_statement:
Let $\overline{H}$ be the matrix appearing in the maxT procedure, let $\iota$ denote the all-ones vector, and define

$$
\overline{h}=\overline{H}\iota.
$$

Suppose that $E$ has independent and identically distributed rows with distribution $\mathcal{N}(0,I)$, and that $\mu_l=\mu_1$ for every $1\leq l\leq p$. Let $Z_1\sim\mathcal{N}(n^{1/2}\mu_1,1)$, and let $Y$ have independent and identically distributed rows with distribution $\mathcal{N}(0,I)$. Writing $q_\alpha^{\overline{h}}$ and $q_\alpha^{\overline{h},Y}$ for the relevant maxT quantiles, **asymptotic power equivalence conjecture.** As $p,n\to\infty$,

$$
\left|\frac{1}{p}\sum_{j=1}^p \mathbb{P}_E\left[n^{1/2}\mu_1+\iota'E_j>q_\alpha^{\overline{h}}\left(n^{1/2}\overline{h}'\iota\mu_1+\max_i\overline{h}'E_i\right)\right]-\mathbb{P}_{Z_1}\left[Z_1>q_\alpha^{\overline{h},Y}\left(n^{1/2}\overline{h}'\iota\mu_1+\max_{1\leq l\leq p}Y_l\right)\right]\right|\to0.
$$

The conjecture asserts that the average rejection probability based on the full error matrix is asymptotically equivalent to the corresponding probability computed using an auxiliary Gaussian matrix. Its validity is presented heuristically in the paper, and no resolution is supplied in the source.
359272.ordinary_assessment: Full simultaneous n,p Gaussian quantile and average power convergence lacks parameter-growth/correlation definitions and a uniform comparison theorem. No choice of a convenient growth regime.

323694.title: Conjecture on the asymptotic dominant orbit of p by 2 by 2 tensors over F_2
323694.literal_statement:
For each positive integer $p$, let the set of $p \times 2 \times 2$ tensors over $\mathbb{F}_2$ have $2^{4p}$ elements, and let $\mathcal{O}$ denote an orbit in this set under the relevant equivalence action. The rank of an orbit is the tensor rank of its elements.

**Asymptotic-orbit conjecture.** As $p$ becomes arbitrarily large, the set of $p \times 2 \times 2$ tensors over $\mathbb{F}_2$ contains a single orbit $\mathcal{O}$ of rank 4 which contains almost all of the $2^{4p}$ tensors:

$$
\lim_{p \to \infty} \frac{|\mathcal{O}|}{2^{4p}} = 1.
$$

The claim predicts that one rank-4 orbit asymptotically dominates the tensor space. It is motivated by the computed cases $p=5$ and $p=6$, in which the rank-4 orbit contains approximately $59.6\%$ and $78.2\%$ of all tensors, respectively; the supplied source gives no resolution.

352603.title: Weak degeneracy lower-bound conjecture for regular graphs
352603.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a $d$-regular graph, and let $
obreak\mathsf{wd}(G)$ denote its weak degeneracy. **Regular-graph weak degeneracy conjecture.** Every $d$-regular graph $G$ satisfies

379438.title: Joyner's conjecture 4.3 on parameters of toric codes
379438.literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}(E,D,X)$ be the toric code associated to the $1$-cycle $E$, the $T$-invariant Cartier divisor $D$, and the toric variety $X$. Assume that $X$ is a nonsingular toric variety of dimension $r$, that

$$
\psi_D(v)=\min_{u\in P_D\cap M}\langle u,v\rangle
$$

is strictly convex, and that $\deg(C)>\deg(D^r)$. **Joyner's conjecture 4.3.** If $q$ is sufficiently large, then every $f\in\mathrm{H}^0(X,\mathcal{O}(D))$ has at most $n$ zeros among the rational points of $X$. Consequently,

$$
k\geq\dim\mathrm{H}^0(X,\mathcal{O}(D))=\#(P_D\cap M),
$$

$$
d\geq n-r!\,\#(P_D\cap M).
$$

Moreover, if $n>r!\,\#(P_D\cap M)$, then

$$
\dim\mathrm{H}^0(X,\mathcal{O}(D))=\#(P_D\cap M).
$$

The paper gives a counterexample for $q\geq8$, so the conjecture is refuted.
379438.ordinary_assessment: Literal itself reports source counterexample q≥8 and inconsistent references dispute it. Actual primary body unread: no authenticated refutation supplied here; no discovery credit.

345820.title: The finite sparse-forcing conjecture
345820.literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal{S}$ be a set of graphs. It is **sparse forcing** if, whenever graphs $G_n$ satisfy $|G_n|\to\infty$, have edge density $p_n=|G_n|^{-o(1)}$, and the limits

$$
c_F=\lim_{n\to\infty}t_{p_n}(F,G_n)
$$

exist for every graph $F$ with $\sup_F c_F^{1/e_F}<\infty$, the condition $c_F=1$ for every $F\in\mathcal{S}$ implies $c_F=1$ for every graph $F$. **Finite sparse-forcing conjecture.** No finite set of graphs $\mathcal{S}$ can be sparse forcing. The paper's counterexample shows that no set of triangle-free graphs is sparse forcing, while this conjecture asserts the stronger impossibility for every finite set.
345820.ordinary_assessment: Must construct bounded normalized densities for every graph simultaneously while matching any finite prescribed set. Dense graphon perturbations face C4 forcing, and no slow-sparse replacement paying all moments obtained.

373205.title: The inverse Littlewood conjecture for structure of low-norm sets
373205.literal_statement:
Let $A\subset\mathbb{Z}$ be a finite set of size $N$, and let $K>0$. Write $1_A$ for its indicator and define

$$
\widehat{1_A}(\theta)=\sum_{n\in A}e(-n\theta),\qquad e(x)=e^{2\pi i x}.
$$

A finite arithmetic progression is a finite subset of $\mathbb{Z}$ with constant nonzero common difference. **The inverse Littlewood conjecture.** If

$$
\\|\widehat{1_A}\\|_1\leqslant K\log N,
$$

then there are integers $m,r\ll_K1$, finite arithmetic progressions $P_1,\ldots,P_m\subset\mathbb{Z}$ of length at most $N$, finite sets $X_1,\ldots,X_r\subset\mathbb{Z}$ with

$$
\left|\bigcup_jX_j\right|=o_K(N),
$$

and $\epsilon_1,\ldots,\epsilon_m,\eta_1,\ldots,\eta_r\in\\{-1,1\\}$ such that

$$
1_A=\sum_{1\leqslant i\leqslant m}\epsilon_i1_{P_i}+\sum_{1\leqslant j\leqslant r}\eta_j1_{X_j}.
$$

This is a proposed structural inverse theorem: it would describe every set with nearly minimal Fourier $L^1$ norm using boundedly many arithmetic progressions, up to a small exceptional union. No counterexample is known; analogous finite-field results are known, and the source notes a related, slightly stronger conjecture of Petridis. The conjecture would in particular imply that $A$ has dense intersection with an arithmetic progression of length at most $N$.
373205.ordinary_assessment: Corpus references say solved while literal says open. Actual primary theorem/proof unread; status conflict not a proof. Bounded signed progression decomposition with o_K(N) exception remains unpaid.

315996.title: Cereceda's conjecture
315996.literal_statement:
For a finite simple undirected graph $G$, the degeneracy of $G$ is the least
integer $d$ such that every non-empty subgraph of $G$ has a vertex of degree at
most $d$. For a positive integer $k$, a proper $k$-colouring of $G$ is a map
$\gamma : V(G) \to \{1,\dots,k\}$ with $\gamma(u) \neq \gamma(v)$ for every edge
$uv \in E(G)$. Two proper $k$-colourings $\gamma, \gamma'$ of $G$ are adjacent
if there is exactly one vertex $v \in V(G)$ with $\gamma(v) \neq \gamma'(v)$;
the reconfiguration graph of proper $k$-colourings of $G$ has as its vertices
all proper $k$-colourings of $G$, with this adjacency.

For every integer $d \ge 1$ there exists a constant $C = C(d)$ such that for
every graph $G$ on $n$ vertices with degeneracy at most
$d$ and every two proper $(d+2)$-colourings $\alpha$ and $\beta$ of
$G$, there is a sequence of proper $(d+2)$-colourings

$$
\alpha = \gamma_0, \gamma_1, \dots, \gamma_\ell = \beta
$$

such that $\gamma_{i-1}$ and $\gamma_i$ differ in the colour of exactly one
vertex for each $i \in \{1,\dots,\ell\}$, and

$$
\ell \le C n^2 .
$$

Equivalently, the reconfiguration graph of proper
$(d+2)$-colourings of an $n$-vertex graph of degeneracy at most
$d$ is connected and has diameter $O(n^2)$, where the implied constant depends
only on $d$.
315996.ordinary_assessment: Low-degree deletion lifts recoloring but naive recurrence multiplies work by d and can be exponential. No global quadratic amortization at exactly d+2 colors; connectivity alone does not pay diameter.

321875.title: The bounded-boxicity conjecture for large-edgewidth graphs on a fixed surface
321875.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph embedded in a fixed surface $\Sigma$. The **edgewidth** of $G$ is the length, measured by the number of edges, of a shortest noncontractible cycle in $G$.

**Large-edgewidth boxicity conjecture.** There exists an integer $e_\Sigma$ such that every graph $G$ embeddable on $\Sigma$ with edgewidth at least $e_\Sigma$ has boxicity at most three.

372435.literal_statement:

320650.title: The asymptotic t-broom conjecture for distance graphs
320650.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $G_k$ denote its distance-$k$ graph, and let $e(G_k)$ be the number of edges of $G_k$. Two graphs are **$k$-isomorphic** when their distance-$k$ graphs are isomorphic; a **$t$-broom** is the graph construction described in the paper, with $t$ broom branches.

**The asymptotic t-broom conjecture.** For every integer $k\geq 3$, there exists a function $h=h(k)$ such that, whenever $n\geq h(k)$, the maximum of $e(G_k)$ over all graphs $G$ with $|G|=n$ is attained when $G$ is $k$-isomorphic to a $t$-broom for some $t$.

The conjecture is motivated by the known extremal result for trees, while the paper notes that small cases can have better constructions, including the $7$-cycle when $(n,k)=(7,3)$. The authors state that they believe the conjecture but cannot prove it.
320650.ordinary_assessment: All fixed k≥3 and sufficiently large n required; C7 small exception cannot refute eventual statement. Need full distance-graph symmetrization or infinite family beating every t-broom; neither obtained.
